What should VISOR call you? Welcome to VISOR. What should I call you? Say your name, or tap Skip.
Which of these describe what you experience? Which of these describe what you experience? You can pick more than one. Say: center loss, side loss, blurry, light sensitivity, or not sure.
Tell me about your vision, in your own words If you\'d like, tell me about your vision in your own words. Anything that doesn\'t fit the boxes. Or tap Skip.
How much does it affect daily life? How much does your vision affect daily life? Say: a little, a moderate amount, or a lot.
How fast should I talk? How fast should I talk? Say: slower, normal, or faster.
How much detail do you want? When I describe things, how much detail do you want? Say: brief, standard, or detailed.
You\'re all set! You\'re all set. You can change any of this later in Settings, or just ask me.

Hazard Awareness Scene Description Reading Assistance
Mattresses lean across the sidewalk ahead. Bags and bedding sit at their base, taking up much of the walking space.
Three low, black, ball-shaped barriers stand on the paved walkway. The nearest is on the right, with two more farther ahead toward the left.
A pile of branches and debris blocks the path directly ahead, beside the metal gate on the right.
A large white planter blocks much of the narrow sidewalk ahead. It stands between the building wall on the left and the street on the right.
Parked bicycles extend into the left side of the sidewalk. Their wheels project into the walking area beside the parked cars.
Steps lead up to the shop door ahead, with handrails on both sides. Two narrow yellow tracks run over the left side of the steps.
Low concrete planters stand across the paved area ahead. Behind them, steps lead up to the entrance on the left.
A concrete pole stands directly ahead in the narrow sidewalk. Bushes on the left and parked motorcycles on the right further narrow the walking space.
A motorcycle and a red chair occupy part of the covered walkway ahead, toward the right. Stacks of coiled tubing and other materials narrow both sides.
A fan and a stool extend into the walkway on the left. A cable lies on the floor beside the fan, and a food cart narrows the right side.
A short set of steps leads up to the sidewalk directly ahead. A second staircase descends beside it on the right, behind a metal railing.
Uneven concrete steps rise along the path ahead. A metal handrail runs along the left side, and a wall borders the right.
Outdoor steps rise ahead, with snow covering parts of the steps and their edges. A metal handrail runs along the right side.
The pavement rises unevenly around a tree directly ahead. Large roots protrude from its base, and a raised slab sits to the right of the trunk.
A broken section of concrete forms a raised edge across the sidewalk ahead. Cracks and loose pieces surround the raised section.
Broken concrete slabs surround an open gap in the sidewalk ahead, near the curb on the right. A metal pole stands beside the gap.
A concrete pole stands ahead near the left edge of the narrow sidewalk. Standing water fills the street beside the curb on the left.
A wide patch of paving is missing from the sidewalk ahead, beside the tree on the right. Exposed ground and broken tile edges interrupt the walking surface.
Loose bricks and gaps interrupt the sidewalk ahead. The paving is broken and uneven beside the grassy edge on the right.
An open hole interrupts the snow-covered sidewalk ahead, slightly to the right. A branch sticks out of the hole.
A waiting room has rows of blue seats in the center, facing toward you. Large windows line the right wall, and glass doors and vending machines are at the far end.
A small waiting room has a wooden bench along the left wall and a drinks vending machine on the right. A blue bin stands between the bench and the machine.
A narrow hall has wood-paneled walls and a high sloping ceiling. Chairs and a curved wooden partition are on the left; windows line the right, with an open doorway at the far end.
A cafe seating area faces a large street-facing window. Small tables stand among armchairs and wooden chairs, with a cushioned bench along the brick wall on the left.
A cafe has wooden tables and chairs on the left. A high table with stools stands against the windows ahead, and a small counter sits beside the glass door on the right.
A cafe has a service counter on the left and rows of tables and wooden chairs ahead. People sit at a table in the center, and another person stands at the counter.
An open-sided seating area has long wooden tables and benches beneath a roof. People sit at the tables, with patterned wooden screens behind them and trees visible outside.
A library has rows of white bookshelves with aisles between them. A computer on a stand labeled Search is in front on the left.
A library has a rectangular table and wooden chairs in front on the right. Rows of tall bookshelves fill the space behind it, with an aisle along the left.
Tall bookshelves line both sides of a narrow carpeted aisle. The aisle leads straight ahead to a wall beneath a row of ceiling lights.
A library has rows of low white shelves filled with media cases. A green-carpeted aisle runs down the center, with windows along the right wall.
A reception area has two wooden desks against the back wall, each with two chairs in front. A table lamp sits on each desk, with tall doorways on either side of the room.
A dining room has a table set with plates and glasses beneath a chandelier. Wooden chairs surround the table, with tall curtained windows behind it and an orange wall on the left.
A supermarket aisle has tall shelves of bottles on both sides. A bottle display stands ahead on the right, with the aisle continuing to its left.
A supermarket aisle has product shelves on both sides and freestanding displays down the middle. Several shoppers stand ahead, beneath a large banner celebrating the coronation.
Store shelves hold bags, boxes, and cans of pet food. Large bags fill the bottom shelf, with smaller packages above and a tiled aisle in front.
A grocery store has low display cases in the center and taller refrigerated cases along the sides. A wide aisle runs along the left, with shoppers farther ahead.
A laundromat has washing machines along the left wall and stacked machines at the far end. A long folding table is on the right, with blue seats behind it against the wall.
A gravel path runs through dense trees and shrubs. A wooden bench sits beside the path on the right, and the path curves to the left farther ahead.
A kitchen has a dark counter with a sink across the front. A cooktop and range hood are at the back left; a refrigerator, microwave, and oven are on the right.

The sign says: Service in Greek and English.

The notice says: Post office open Monday and Friday, a.m. It does not give exact opening or closing times.

The menu says: Sausage, egg, and melted cheddar on a toasted English muffin.
The sign says: Enter. Library and community centre. An arrow points to the left.
The sign says: John Marshall Library. Fairfax County Public Library.
The notice says: Smoking is prohibited in the rooms. Use designated smoking areas.

The sign says: Please close gate. Footpath.
The reminder says: Please remember. There is no flush. Take all rubbish home with you.
